item.title: Seeking Greenlights
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Page Layout: Standard SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: This SCP is a garden center of an abandoned hardware store. Containment is a faux construction site around the garden center. While external measurements only read 100 meters by 150 meters, measurements from the inside put it at 1.5 kilometers by 2 kilometers. The garden center is always full of plants, which change depending on the season. In spring, flowers are found throughout the center. In Summer vegetables are found In Fall, pumpkins and gourds are found. In Winter, Evergreen trees are found. Besides normal plants, unknown and anomalous varieties have been found. Inside the garden center, humanoid creatures roam the place. These creatures, while all distinctly human looking and having different physical features, all wear the employee uniform of the hardware store and will ask how they can help when approached. They are docile, but will attack an individual in self defense or if someone has damaged any of the plants inside.

Central Narrative: The main narrative is of exploration and interacting with the humanoids inside the SCP.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: My concept is unique because it changes with the seasons. While somewhat similar to other SCP's with increased interior size and humanoids within, the space in my concept is finite, and the humanoids docile until attacked. Another unique part of my concept is the anomalous plants and unknown means of where the plants come from.

item.title: Re: Time: Limited
item.content:encoded:
My main concern is the fact that you plan to spend a good chunk of the narrative describing how this alien race destroys themselves containing this ‘mass’, only for the ending to pivot and depict the mass as a god-chatting pacifist that wouldn’t harm a fly. To put it another way, it seems like there are two stories here, told one after the other.

Yea you've got a hell of a point. The reasoning for the mass' change is that it encountered another space-faring being that essentially "taught" the mass of exploration and "the beauty of the universe" so to speak. The relation is intended to be that the mass was like a child lashing out and needed to be taught morality. There is meant to be uncertainty as to if the mass is simply being manipulative or not. If it serves the narrative better I'll focus more on the transmissions.

I’m also a bit confused about the origin of the mass. You explicitly state that an activated latent gene causes it early on, then cap off your comment by suggesting Yaldabaoth caused it instead. Is this intentional? If so, why the ambiguity?

I worded badly. The activation of the gene is due to a technology based in sarkicism. Aliens mix sarkicism with technology and end up activating this gene. The gene "unlocks a species true form", or at least that's what the mass ends up implying to the foundation. I do apologise if I failed to explain anything properly.

item.title: [Seeking Greenlight]: Objective Beauty
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Drama/Emotional

Page Layout (Optional): Plot development wil occur within various addenda

Elevator Pitch: Objective Beauty is a male humanoid, appearing to anyone who sees him as the most beautiful thing they have ever seen. Seeing Objective Beauty makes one forget all their former passions and interests and obsess about Objective Beauty. He himself is not malicious; he hates having this condition, he feels guilty when someone gets harmed because of him, and is very cooperative in general (class: very much safe)

Central Narrative: Objective Beauty is found having been ''kidnapped'' by his obsessed parents until the age of 17. Research begins on the nature of his changing appearance based on who sees him (one theory being his particles being in a complex superposition). Several researchers commit suicide after seing Objective Beauty; it is possible to wipe Objective Beauty out of one's memory, but this will leave them extremely nihilistic, as if they still know they had seen him and cannot remember him anymore. Several tests are completed with D-class suffering from mental illness and different types of animals, maybe even other SCP's. Objective Beauty grows more and more depressed when more tests offer the same outcome. often asking to be euthanized; this causes regular discussion within the Foundation ethics-commitee.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The deteriorating mental state of Objective Beauty, which worsens after each test resulting in either a death or an extremely potent memory wipe, leaving the memory wiped person as a shell of their former selves.

Additional Notes: The existence of Objective Beauty sparks a philosophical debate within certain departments of the Foundation, leaving a large number of personnel nihilistic, even though they have never seen Objective Beauty itself.

item.title: Re: Shepherd boy
item.content:encoded:
[+] Overall
[-] Overall

My biggest issue with this is that a lot of the writing is not good: I'd really advise running this through an automated checker like e.g. libreoffice writer so you can catch easy to find mistakes like the lack of capitalisation etc. I've tried to highlight as much as I can here but I have almost certainly missed stuff cos there's just…a lot.

Beyond this, the jump between the exploration logs and the interview is too big: there's no connective writing between them so it just feels…too sudden? Like in part because -2 doesn't show up in the explorations at all and in part because thre's not really like, any reference to the events of the explorations in it or anything so it's just…there?

The actual exploration logs are fine but they feel…a little directionless? I don't think this is necessarily an issue so much as the slight lack of focus on the interesting events: two people being grabbed by a snake feels like it should be a huge focal event, rather than something which kinda happens in the background, y'know?

It also kinda feels like a lot of this is building up without a clear direction: that might be easier to introduce once you've written more of it, it's hard to tell; but it doesn't feel like all the elements are going to come together in some kind of satisfying conclusion yet.

[-] Overall
[+] Line By Line
[-] Line By Line

Gonna note that I can miss stuff; flag things which are right as being wrong and indeed flag things which are deliberately wrong.
I'll likely use strikethrough to indicate stuff to remove and green text to indicate stuff to add.

The abandoned Mining factory in ██████ ███████, Mongolia

I'd probably name this place: anyone with clearance to see this file almost certainly has clearance to see where it is; otherwise how would they know where to go.

Also this image is ~4MB in size and pretty tiny in the page: I'd recommend opening it in an image editing program and downscaling it (you can ask in #site11 on IRC if you're having difficulty with this)

Item #: SCP-XXXX

I wouldn't necessarily bother including the Item # and Object Class lines at the start if you're using a header that includes them too.

Containment Area M21 is to be located in 300m deep underground ofin the Gobi desert in Mongolia.

I would probably specify that SCP-XXXX-2 is to be stored in this containment area, or at least tie it into the SCP file more.

The 'to be' is technically fine but generally it's advised to say what the Containment Procedures are, rather than should be. 'deep' is to be cut because we can assume that "300m underground" means "down" and it feels clunky here.

SCP-XXXX-2 is to be held in a 5 m cube made of entirely Tungsten metal, the walls are to be (50m) thick on each side, with no gap for planetary or organic life to enter.

My concern with this is that it's a lot of detail that doesn't feel important: the exact size and thickness of the cube aren't really that important; and neither is the exact material it's made of; particularly since none of this detail is referenced later.

Something like:

SCP-XXXX-2 is held in a tungsten cube that cannot be accessed.

Would be clearer and conciser.

The air ventilation of the cell will be 3000 miles (4828.032 kilometers) in length away from the cell and to be checked three times a week.

The foundation always uses metric (so no miles figure) and I would not specify the length to that precision, or indeed, any precision generally? Also like…3000 miles is really far: like, for reference, Tokyo is 1877 miles from Ulaanbaatar and Manila is 2434 miles from Ulaanbaatar.

If any of humanoids that resides in SCP-XXXX-1 are to move from their respective station

'humanoids' feels odd here: I believe the people you are referring to are actually humans? 'respective station' is odd: generally in english, station refers to either 'position in society' or like 'a train station', so 'position' would be better than 'respective station'.

they are to be immediately apprehended and held in the same containment cell as SCP-XXXX and is questioned for further notice.

Do you mean SCP-XXXX-2 here? Also 'questioned for further notice' doesn't make sense; I'd likely used 'interrogated' in place of 'questioned' and I'd probably cut the 'for further notice' completely.

I'd also strongly suggest putting them in a separate containment chamber; and reordering so it's "immediately apprehended and interrogated before being held in the…"

No more than five personnel, wearing in Hazmat suits, are to enter SCP-XXXX-1 at the same time time.

Specifying 'at the same time' prevents the implication that only five people can ever enter.

and no unauthorized personnel and civilian are to be in the proximity of the area or enter SCP-XXXX-1

this can be assumed: they are unauthorized so they are not allowed in.

Unauthorized personnel under level 5 entering the area without permission are given Class C amnestic and is reassigned to a different project. Civilian is to given Class-A amnestic, and is to quarantined based on the severity of their bodily form and psyche.

I'd cut this; we don't need to know how they're punished and we can assume folk who access without permission are to be punished.

In the event of a Containment Breach

"Containment Breach" doesn't need to be capitalised here.

all on sight researchers

'site': 'sight' is 'vision'

or to stay in shelter until the MTF Theta-4 ("Gardeners") are to arrive at the facility and apprehended the entity.

SCP-CXXX consists of two components; a cave (SCP-XXXX-1) and a humanoid protecting it (SCP-XXXX-2).

I would generally avoid defining SCP-XXXX in this way because it forces you to refer to -1 and -2 a lot and means you almost never refer to the whole. In this case, I'd likely define -2 as the base anomaly and leave the cave as -1.

The semi-colon (;) should be a colon here (:) too technically but I think the first change means you don't need to worry about this.

SCP-XXXX-2 resembles a small Hun human male in his mid-teens, standing 169 cm (5,5) and weight around 55 kg (123 lbs).

Again, foundation only uses metric so don't include the imperial conversions here. This said: his exact height and weight aren't important for a reader to understand the anomaly so I'd probably just cut this. I'd also avoid using 'resembles' and other vague words: just say he is a human here even if he's a human with anomalous properties.

Back hair and brown eyes.

This is a sentence fragment (i.e, the issue is it contains no verb: something like "SCP-XXXX-2 has black hair and brown eyes" would be clearer, though if you do cut the height/weight in the last sentence, you could refer to these at the end of the sentence. I'm also assuming 'Back hair' was a typo for 'Black hair'.

Footnote 1: A deel (Mongolian: дээл [deːɮ]; Buryat: дэгэл, [dɛɡɛɮ]) is an item of traditional clothing commonly worn since centuries ago among the Mongols and other nomadic tribes of Central Asia, including various Turkic peoples, and can be made from cotton, silk, wool, or brocade

This isn't a very good description of what a deel is because it entirely focuses on who wears it and what it's made from; whereas if you're putting a footnote in to explain what it is, you want to focus on 'what does it look like'.

It also looks like it's ripped from wikipedia: this is fine but you will have to cite it if so. I recommend checking out the Image Use Policy here since it talks a lot about how to ensure material is compatible with the wiki's license and how to attribute the images; whilst wikipedia words aren't an image, the same policy applies here.

which has been ripped and thronetorn, however, SCP-XXXX-2 refused##greens## to change it.

Instance of SCP-XXXX-2 anomalies properties, are manifestation of Reptilian (Saurosida) entity strongly resembling a dragon made out of natural components.

The start of this is kinda a mess; I'd probably suggest rephrasing to e.g.:

SCP-XXXX-2 has the ability to manifest entities made out of natural components which resemble a dragon

That said: "natural components" is super vague; and it might be worth specifying if this is Chinese style dragons or Western style dragons

Its full length is impossible to measure but is hypothesized to be between 1000 and 2000 kilometers.

"Its" is unclear if you mean "SCP-XXXX-2" or "the entity"; I'd probably use 'unknown' in place of 'impossible to measure' because it seems to me that it'd be easy to measure this theoretically if it stood still. I'd also use 'estimated' in place of 'hypothesized' here.

1000 and 2000 kilometers is also too big. Like…godzilla is maybe 300m tall at most (it varies depending on the film; usually 100m is closer to the average), which means this thing is 5000 godzillas long at minimum and likely 15000 godzilla's long using the average godzilla height)

SCP-XXXX-1 is a Cognitohazardous cave under a destroyed and abandoned Mining factory

neither cognitohazardous nor mining should be capitalised here. I would probably only use one of 'destroyed' and 'abandoned' here since there's a lot of overlap in their meaning. Also 'cognitohazardous' is super broad and you really do have to specify how here; or just…not mention the properties at all.

it is measured to be around 4000 kilometers deep

4000km deep takes you through the crust of the earth (30km thick) and the mantle of the earth (2900 km thick) and into the outer core of the planet.

The deepest mine in the world, currently, is the Mponeng gold mine. It extends about 4km deep, or around 1/1000th of the depth of this mine.

Like I get this is like…anomalous and stuff but it does not feasible for the mine to be this deep without this being a lot more of a big deal than it currently is.

However, how big SCP-XXXX-omega mass is impossible to measure.

what is SCP-XXXX-omega? This is one of the only two places here you mention it and you never define it.

The other place implies they can enter SCP-XXXX-omega which makes measuring it's mass feel weird? So I'd probably cut this but??

SCP-XXXX-1 resides a snake-like creature approximately 200 kilometers, maybe even bigger.

'maybe even bigger' is real casual and I would not include it. Rephrasing to lead with the snake creature would be clearer e.g.: "A snake-like creature approximately 200km long resides in SCP-XXXX". Again though, 200km is really big to the point where if you said 2km, I would say it's probably too big still.

About fifty kilometers down, there is a massive field stretching further from the human eye

'stretching further than the human eye can see' is a good metaphor to grasp for but this is a SCP description: you want to describe things objectively using set sizes rather than vague things like 'larger than can be seen'

filled with stationary humanoids varies in ages, they're made out of natural components, different species of flowers but growing in the same root

this feels…muddled. It probably needs to be a few sentences to make it read right but I'm not exactly sure how best to do that.

Picture of a wooden horse taken during the second exploration

I'd probably move this into the second exploration

The instants of SCP-XXXX-1's anomalous properties became apparent when entering the area.

I'm not sure what you mean by 'instants' here but it feels like this would be better as 'SCP-XXXX-1's anomalous properties become…'

Then again, 'anomalous properties' is the kinda super vague statement I'd generally urge folk to avoid cos it can be basically anything; it'd be more effective to say something like "Radio signals cut off inside SCP-XXXX-1" say.

It is hypnotized that SCP-XXXX-1 refracts of all organic structures, even humans and animals, but it is yet to be backed up.

'hypnotized' should be 'hypothesized'. I'm not sure what you're getting at with 'refracts': maybe like, 'restructures all organic structures' or 'reshapes' or something? 'refracts' is a phenomenon where light changes direction when it enters a partially transparent material and unlikely to be what you're looking for here.

SCP-XXXX was discovered by serious of civilian interviews and gossips in ███████ ████████ after the mass destruction of major mining facilities.

'SCP-XXXX was discovered during the investigation of the destruction of mining facilities in [place name].'

As before, redacting the place name here is a bad idea and you should just name a place here.

It is noted that the SCP-XXXX-2 was already known amongst the locals as a fairy tale hero, with SCP-XXXX-1 mentioned multiple times during the interviews indicating they're might be connected in some way.

'fairy tale hero' feels super casual here; maybe make mention of it appearing in local mythology instead? Also it feels like this needs to setup a firmer connection spatially between the mine and -1 (as in, where is -1 in relation to the mine?) and a firmer connection between -2 and -1.

The investigation into the origins of SCP-XXXX-1 and its relation with SCP-XXXX-2 is ongoing.

Due to the unknown nature of SCP-XXXX-1, MTF-Zeta-9 (Mole Rats) were sendsent in to explore the cave and return with the sample.

'deployed' would be more clinical than 'sent in'; and 'return with the sample' needs additional detail to indicate what kinda samples they're looking for: at the moment it's just…kinda vague.

However they did not return in time, and Recovery team was dispatched to collect the remaining of the team.

This feels like it should be after the first exploration log; rather than spoiling that they don't return immediately before like…getting to the log, y'know? Same goes for the rest of this paragraph.

Something like "After they had not returned 8 hours later, a recovery team was dispatched to investigate" would flow better; with the option of increasing 8 hours or decreasing it depending on how you feel.

They found MTF-Zeta-9 (Mole Rats) team's all none organic materials like guns, vest, and food cans some completely full and other empty.

Something like "Only the non-organic components of MTF Zeta-9's equipment were found." would be clearer; you don't need to specify the mole rats every time just, y'know, to cut down the length.

Date: █/██20██

I wouldn't redact this either; knowing when this happened is important contextualisation for how long the events took to play out etc.

Subject: inside of SCP-XXXX-1

I'd cut this; there's not really a subject so you don't need to say this.

Team Members: Agents Luna, Ouyulan, Zachary, and Sunder.

Agent Olson: Command, we are entering SCP-XXXX-omega.

same comment about -omega not being defined as earlier; I think you're wanting -1 here?

Command: Roger that! stay in touch as long as you can!

I'd avoid using ! as much as possible: the more you use it, the less emphasis it carries. Also it's the end of a sentence, so the 'stay' after the first should be capitalised.

the five agents began to hike down the cave, the light started to dim away.

Capitalised start of sentences, even here.

you and Agent Sunder grew up closerclose to here, right?

Yup the real countryside pumpkin is me.

do you mean 'bumpkin' here? 'country' would read better than 'countryside' too

not sure what you're trying to imply by 'mouth by mouth forum'; perhaps 'it was spread via word of mouth'?

QuiteQuiet, any of you heard anything?

the ground started to shake and small rubble falls on top of Agent Zachary's head! Olson looked up, there was long intervened vines and roots seemingly identical to a snake skeleton.

'rubble' is collective; I think you want like 'a small rock' here? 'intervened' is probably meant to be 'intertwined' or 'tangled'?

TIME: Corrupted

Ending on the time feels kinda janky here; like…why would it be presented here and not earlier? or like, throughout this since this log takes place over an hour or so

At least we have natural light! I reckon the snake attacked us because of our light.

why are none of them questioning why there is natural light deep within a mine

or does the air is less timid than when we eventually hiked down

'or is the air less timid than when we started' would be clearer though…timid is not the word you're looking for here. I'm not sure what the right word is though.

Agent Olson gets up and looks around and breathing in and out slowly.

I'd replace the second and with a comma

The camera pans out to a giant field filled with what seems to be an ecosystem.

…how does the camera pan out? Why did no-one notice it before since this is implied to be right there since it's just…the camera showing it?

than the animal above

'than animals above ground'

There are very big threes

trees?

The light source of this… the place is completely natural, I have no idea where the sun is even shining from the top of us.

How do they know the light source is natural? It seems like they have no idea where the light is coming from here

But the air becoming even timider than the last cave we were in.

…do you mean 'thinner'?

His cough becomes more severe as he goes.

'as he goes' is missing like a 'towards the light' kinda thing where it says where he's going, y'know?

Also this is bolded instead of italicised

Suddenly Olson turned back and saw a hill fill with flowers, he didn't see before

These should be impartial records of what happened: words like 'Suddenly' feel really out of place here; and 'he didn't see before' should be conveyed via what he says rather than the transcript assuming it.

oh fuck, maybe that place is forcing my allergies to kick me in the balls.

This feels weird like the implication is the hill is far away and unlikely to be the source of the coughing? It seems pollen from the nearby plants would be a much more believable explanation here

Once they were at the top of the hill, the camera zoom to an enormous Yurt, behind the Yurt what seemed to be humanoids, stationary.

I again would not refer to the camera doing stuff; generally an MTF will want to keep hands free so this is more…passive body camera recording than active filming, y'know?

Yurt also should not be capitalised here; and this should probably be a few sentences where they like, explicitly walk around the yurt a little or something so they can see the humanoids

But this one… seems incredible (coughs) a saturated.

I'm not sure what you're trying to get at with 'a saturated' here

they're all people!

on a bee made out of natural components sitting on a yellow flower

this phrasing implies there's something special about a bee being made of natural components but bees are y'know, already made of natural components

And yet… this thing hadhas already taken a life.

Why 'a' life? Like, there's four members of his team who have disappeared so far; and like there's room for him to be uncertain about some of them but only in two people pairs so he has to think either 0, 2 or 4 of them are dead

But I want to ask you seriousa series of questions.

Its alright, but we have estimated that your age is about 2000 years.

What led them to this estimate?

It was quitequiet for three minutes.

[-] Line By Line

item.title: Re: Greenlight - To Go Hell and Back
item.content:encoded:
Okay, I'm digging a lot of the changes you've applied here. I do, however, have a few questions for my own edification.

First of all, why does the MTF die? Canon is, of course, fully malleable, but I believe it would take quite an offensive force to kill off a team of well-armed individuals specifically trained in anomalous exploration like this. What does their deaths contribute to the story as a whole?

Now, this may be a silly question, but bear with me. Why are the demons doing this? I know it can be easy to use entities like that as antagonistic props, but even the most rudimentary of motives would help flesh them out.

Outside of that, my main concern here is the presence what I usually term as "exploration log bloat": an exploration log that's mostly idle chatter between its participants with actual plot points few and far between. That's a problem for the draft crit stage, though.

Overall, I think these are questions and concerns that can be smoothed out in the process. The actual core concept has a real human struggle and a classical twist that's been adapted well to the setting. With that in mind, I'm giving this a greenlight. Good luck!

item.title: The Flooding Well (Looking for Greenlights)
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Horror

Page Layout: Normal description and containment procedures, but also plan on writing two expedition logs, a discovery log and an incident report.

Elevator Pitch: SCP-XXXX is a well located in a forest somewhere in south England, that on 60 to 80 hour intervals will fill up and flood with a slime (SCP-XXXX-1) that is extremely sticky and hard to control, except using methods of incineration. This slime will attempt to consume any biological matter it can find to grow itself. If SCP-XXXX-1's path is blocked for long enough, it'll go back down the well, reverting the effects of SCP-XXXX-A.

Central Narrative: The SCP is discovered after countless reports from trekkers in the area that they saw corpses with slime oozing out of every orifice in their body, and field agents are immediately dispatched to look around the area. Of course, only one of them returns safely, requesting backup, and soon after countless attempts at containment, incineration proves to work. This situation is less than favorable for the foundation, as SCP-XXXX's secrecy is easily breached, and they immediately attempt to block off the forest to everyone.

Hook / Attention Grabber: I want this article's real taste and horror to come from the Expedition logs, in which the inside of SCP-XXXX is explored, and countless new things about the true origin of the SCP come to light.

Additional Notes: I think that while the SCP's main idea may be a bit bland, that with a little bit of work and criticism, it could be refined, so constructive feedback is heavily requested and appreciated.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Page Layout: Standard Format

Elevator Pitch: Imagine if you take a walk in the forest silent and you see a random black box just sitting there you feel no attraction to it until you hear it knock twice, your suddenly now just have to look at that box you don't know why you have to always look at it but it just feels like you should. Again the box knocks and this time you go to the box standing right next to you glee with excitement and you open the box a holy light shines through like a video game chest and… you dropped to the ground, the box closes and you die of a heart attack.

After random increments of time the box begins knocking at the first 5 knocks the subject just simply examines the box, but after the 6th knock subject forcefully decide to open the box any attempts to stop said subject has always failed. subject that are going to open the box seem to not be affected by any sort of damage until said heart attack occurs. item.title: Re: SCP idea- Leviathan of The midnight Sun (Mitternachtsonne)
item.content:encoded:
Hey there Anonymousauthor, I’ll be critting your idea today!
Note that I am not an official reviewer, so take what I say with a grain of salt. With that being said, let’s begin the crit!

+ Open Section-by-Section
Wooooosh

Elevator Pitch

So your SCP is some kind of large aquatic creature (nice physical description btw). However, I have much the same concerns as Captain Cold in regards to how the Foundation knows it’s appearance so well. Not only this, but why are they such problems associated with looking at it? Is it cognitohazardous? Also:

[…]located somewhere in the Atlantic at a Site known as The Ring.

I would have assumed you meant in or around the Ring of Fire, but that’s in the Pacific. So where is this Ring? And why was it constructed?

Central Narrative

You explain the abilities of this Leviathan in more detail here, where it mutates the surrounding sea life and makes them hostile. Unfortunately, this feels… very similar to SCP-3069, in that the anomaly mutates all surrounding sea life. Not only this, but like Angryman22 and Captain Cold I am concerned about this narrative, which seems to consist only of research missions ending in death. I’d recommend changing it.

Hook/Attention Grabber

Ok, but why can it alter the salinity around itself? This just seems like an extra ability tacked onto the anomaly in order to increase the pressure it puts on the Foundation.

+ Open General Thoughts
I don’t know about this

The idea is similar in ability to SCP-3069, the narrative is cliche and uninteresting, and the hook adds an extra ability randomly, making the whole thing feel a bit disjointed.

As an extra explanation for the narrative, explorations that end in death are completely fine (I actually have a soft spot for them myself). However, people usually expect some kind of twist, deeper narrative, or reveal in these exploration logs, so work on that.

I’d recommend three things:
1. Find something to seperate this concept from SCP-3069.
2. Work on your narrative! Brainstorm ideas, think of an emotion you want your readers to feel, and let that guide the direction your story takes.
3. Check out the Guide Hub for some great essays on ideation and story-ing!

And finally, to sum up your concept in one sentence1:
A large leviathan-like creature (presumably cognitohazardous) that mutates all the surrounding sea life and increases the salinity of the water surrounding it, with devastating effects on its environment.

Anyway, that’s it for my crit today. Thanks for reading, and I hope this helps!

Footnotes
1. This is to help you get an idea of the bare bones of what a critter sees when they read your summary. You may find something you don’t like here, or that we’re getting the wrong impression.

item.title: Re: Jetboat Sights and Adventures: Come Join the Extradimensional Fun!
item.content:encoded:
Hey Manhattan!

Got a bit of critique for you. First of all, I'll start with some of the more technical and grammatical issues.

+ show block
– hide block

"Observations have lead to believe that the clarity of the water is anomalouslyt obscrued from biological and mechanical vision." - It's anomalously obscured (minor spelling error). Also, you wouldn't say "biological and mechanical vision", the word vision is barely ever used when it comes to machines or items. Usually the word "detection" might be used. The whole sentence is really wonky to read. It jumps all over the place in terms of being very formal (like saying biological and mechanical vision) to being extremely informal (lead to believe). Also, saying "lead to believe" without a clear reference to who is being lead to believe sounds really wonky as well.

"Water from SCP-XXXX and Huka falls are chemically incompatible." Something being chemically incompatible means that they'll react if brought together (usually exothermically). Since I don't think that's the case here, a better term would be "insolvent", if you mean that they simply don't mix.

"Cross referencing has revealed that all fourteen unidentified species are related to avian, reptilic, and aquatic species." - You can't really "cross reference" when you're talking about animals. I even tried to look it up and found no reference to that term being used in conjunction with species.

Also, "avian, reptilic and aquatic species" is a really weird way to arrange species. Avian and Reptilian are both what is referred to as "animal classes", a subdivision of the Chordata phylum. There is no "aquatic" animal class. There's three classes of fish, one class of amphibians, and mammals which are occasionally aquatic. So you have one animal class listed, then another animal class, and then a vague term that covers potentially 5 animal classes.

Another thing that really irked me, that line basically described 6 out of the 7 animal classes under the Chordata phylum, pretty much all animals except mammals. But then in the story, there's a horned rat.. a mammal. So you give a description that includes 6 out of the 7 animal classes, and then in the story the animal is actually from that 7th. class not included.

"large increase of noise from human vocal cords." from the video log is also extremely wonky. First of all, you would say "increase IN", not increase of. Secondly, when transcribing a video log, you'd never use the term "noise from human vocal chords". You'd simply say "Shouting", "Screaming", "Chanting" or whatever else the people are doing. It's a much shorter word, and much more accurately describes the sounds being made. When you transcribe a video, your aim is always clarity and brevity. "Noise from human vocal chords" gives me virtually no information, especially compared to how much space it takes up.

If you want to aim for the more formal and scientific sounding tone, you really need a bit of research on the words you use.

Also, why isn't the Foundation keeping any kind of guard over these sites? What's preventing the Foundation from exploring them themselves?

About the story in general, I was a bit confused about who I'm rooting for here. Namid seems entirely passive and is quickly removed. Jack Bennett seems fairly aggressive and not entirely likeable from his monologues. I'm generally quite confused over what the real point of the story is. The SCP phenomena aren't really described in any kind of detail, and the people aren't either.

The premise itself could work, but the tone seems all wrong. The idea of a travelling agency that sells tickets to go to a number of SCPs that they've discovered, that could be a fun concept. The travel agency might be slightly clueless as to the exact nature of the SCPs, it could easily be a fun and light-hearted story.

When it's played straight, it doesn't really seem to work that well. The wondrous aspects are glossed over, and we're left with an angry man ranting on a boat.
